extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for BMJ and other medical journals (current and prospective reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and description of a BMJ training programme and online training pack aimed at teaching peer reviewers what editors want, how to appraise research, and how to produce high-quality reviews. Includes workshop details and reflections on the evidence for training effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of state of peer review research
rubrics_metrics.description: Training aim: 'to tell participants about the state of peer review research.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMJ published a free package of learning material (http://bmj.com/advice/peer_review/) to convey current research on peer review; workshops and self-teaching materials will present this background to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on what constitutes a good review
rubrics_metrics.description: Training aim: 'to make clear to them what constitutes a good review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The training package and workshops are intended to articulate the features editors consider to make a review 'good' (the editorial announces this as an explicit objective, though specific review-item checklists are not listed on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding what matters to BMJ editors about reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Training aim: 'to help them understand what matters to BMJ editors about reviews.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops will include BMJ editors so reviewers learn editorial priorities directly; aligning reviewer reports with editors' needs is an explicit goal of the programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to produce good reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Training aim: 'to help them to produce good reviews.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials are designed for practical skills development (self-teaching pack and half day workshops) so reviewers can apply appraisal skills to produce higher quality reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of reviewers' reports (measured outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: The randomised controlled trial 'showed that training was feasible and yielded some improvements in the quality of reviewers' reports.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The observed benefits were slight and not sustained, indicating modest short-term gains in report quality from very short training interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic expectation of training effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial authors concluded: 'very short training has only a marginal impact. We cannot therefore, recommend use of the intervention we studied.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMJ nevertheless decided to offer the intervention as a service and for potential ancillary benefits; users should expect only marginal/short-lived improvements from brief interventions and further research/evaluation is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer engagement and enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant feedback: 'most participants said during formal feedback that they enjoyed the training.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enjoyment is presented as a positive outcome that may support recruitment and retention of reviewers even if objective quality gains are small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using training for recruitment, information, and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: BMJ's operational rationale: 'training is a potentially important way for us to recruit, inform, and retain good reviewers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is framed not only as quality-improvement but also as an editorial strategy to build and sustain a reviewer pool; workshops are offered periodically and places allocated (first come, first served).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training must not worsen review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The trial 'showed that the intervention did not worsen the quality of reviews.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of harm from training is used to justify offering it despite only marginal benefit; monitoring quality post-training remains implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative improvement of training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The package 'is not set in stone: we will expect to amend it in response to further evaluation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training materials should be updated based on evaluation results and ongoing experience; the programme is presented as adaptable and subject to refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for direct dialogue with editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops 'will also give reviewers the chance to quiz BMJ editors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Face-to-face sessions (half day workshops) are intended to allow reviewers to ask editors questions directly, facilitating clarification of expectations and interactive learning.
